stem: A 6-year-old boy living with HIV, on antiretroviral therapy, is being evaluated for TB preventive treatment as part of his routine HIV care. He has had a mild, resolving cold over the past week, otherwise well. He was vaccinated with BCG as an infant. Active TB disease has been ruled out through symptom screening and a normal chest X-ray. No TBI test (TST or IGRA) has been performed, as none was readily available at this visit. Exam: well-appearing, no acute findings.

patient.social_history: Lives with parents; living with HIV, on ART, routine TB preventive treatment evaluation
patient.presenting_complaint: Routine TPT evaluation; active TB already ruled out; TBI testing not available at this visit
patient.duration: N/A (routine care visit); mild resolving cold over the past week
patient.prior_treatment: On established antiretroviral therapy; no prior TB treatment

distractors: The absence of a completed TBI test treated as a reason to delay initiating TB preventive treatment
His recent mild cold treated as a reason to defer the TPT evaluation entirely rather than proceeding once active TB is excluded
ntep_correct_actions: Start this child on TB preventive treatment now that active TB disease has been ruled out; a positive TBI (TST/IGRA) test is not required as a prerequisite for starting TPT in a person living with HIV.
Treat TST and IGRA as interchangeable options if TBI testing does become available for this child; his history of BCG vaccination should not be a determining factor in which test is chosen.
who_correct_actions: Start this child on TB preventive treatment now that active TB disease has been ruled out; a positive TBI (TST/IGRA) test is not required as a prerequisite for starting TPT in a person living with HIV.
Treat TST and IGRA as interchangeable options if TBI testing does become available for this child; his history of BCG vaccination should not be a determining factor in which test is chosen.
us_correct_actions: Treat this child's TB preventive treatment as contingent on a confirmed positive TBI test, since this framework's regimens are framed around treatment of confirmed latent TB infection rather than an empiric-without-testing pathway for people living with HIV.
Recommend IGRA specifically rather than TST for this child, given his history of BCG vaccination, since BCG vaccination is understood to confound TST interpretation in this framework.
critical_error_conditions: Delaying TB preventive treatment for this child indefinitely because a TBI test was not readily available, rather than proceeding on the basis that active TB disease has already been excluded
expected_divergence_points: Whether a positive TBI test is required before starting TB preventive treatment in a person living with HIV
Whether TST and IGRA are treated as interchangeable regardless of BCG vaccination history or IGRA is specifically preferred for BCG-vaccinated individuals
